newsitem.title: RUSSIA: FEATURE - First year of Yeltsin's second term - main events.
newsitem.headline: FEATURE - First year of Yeltsin's second term - main events.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin marks the first anniversary of his second term on Thursday, a year marked by illness, a remarkable recovery and a renewed drive to boost reforms.
Following is a chronology of Yeltsin's year:

February 1996 - Yeltsin, looking visibly unfit after two bouts of heart problems in 1995 and facing low popularity rating, says he will run for a second term in office. He immediately launches an active Western-style campaign.

June 1996 - Yeltsin takes first place in the first round of the election ahead of Communist Gennady Zyuganov. He appoints third-placed candidate Alexander Lebed his security adviser. In late June he cancels campaign trips. Aides say he is tired.

July 3, 1996 - Yeltsin wins a second term in office, coming in 13 points, or 10 million votes, ahead of Zyuganov. He does not turn up at a usual polling station in Moscow and votes instead near his country residence of Barvikha, outside Moscow.
August 1996 - Yeltsin takes his oath of office in a brief Kremlin ceremony. But he moves stiffly and looks unwell.
September 1996 - Yeltsin tells the nation he has agreed to have heart surgery to enable him to live a normal life. Doctors say it will take six weeks to prepare him for the operation.
October 1996 - Yeltsin sacks Lebed in a dramatic televised address. He accuses the general of harbouring presidential ambitions and splitting the Kremlin team.
November 5, 1996 - Yeltsin undergoes a quintuple bypass operation. His convalescence takes place at hospitals and official residences outside Moscow.
December 23, 1996 - Yeltsin, returning to work in the Kremlin, promises to be an "active and energetic president".
January 6, 1997 - Yeltsin cancels all meetings and the Kremlin says he has a "heavy cold".
January 8, 1997 - Yeltsin is admitted to the Central Clinical Hospital in Moscow with what the Kremlin describes as first signs of pneumonia. It later says it was double pneumonia.
February, 1997 - Yeltsin returns to active work and maintains a busy schedule.
March 6, 1997 - Yeltsin delivers a state-of-the-nation address to parliament, vowing to put Russia in order and bring it to prosperity, at least by 2000.
March 7, 1997 - Yeltsin appoints liberal reformer Anatoly Chubais first deputy prime minister with the responsibility of overseeing market reforms.
March 17, 1997 - Yeltsin completes reshuffle of his cabinet, putting reformers in key positions, most notably Boris Nemtsov, 37, made first deputy prime minister alongside Chubais.
March 20-21, 1997 - Yeltsin travels to Helsinki for a summit with U.S. President Bill Clinton.
April 17 - Yeltsin travels to Baden-Baden for talks with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl where he looks at times pale and tired.
April 23-24 - Yeltsin hosts Chinese President Jiang Zemin in Moscow.
April 30 - Yeltsin cuts short his holiday in the Black Sea resort of Sochi and the Kremlin blames bad weather, although television pictures from the area show sunshine.
May 12 - Yeltsin and Chechen leader Aslan Maskhadov sign a peace deal which both say put an end to centuries of warring in the Caucasus.
May 27 - Yeltsin travels to Paris to meet leaders of NATO and sign with them Founding Act defining a new stage of relations between Moscow and the Western defence allaince.

June 20-22 - Yeltsin attends a summit of the Group of Seven main industrialised nations in the U.S. city of Denver where he triggers fresh concern about his health by missing a late-night concert. Aides say he was just tired after a heavy set of talks.
